classes.name: Elección directa de presidente y vicepresidente
classes.note: President and vice president run on one ticket in a single national district. Under the 1994 Constitution (arts. 94-98) a ticket wins in the first round with more than 45% of the valid affirmative votes, or 40% and a lead of more than 10 points; otherwise the top two meet in a runoff 30 days later (2015 and 2023; in 2003 the runoff was called but not held because one ticket withdrew). Four-year term, one consecutive re-election. The two elections of 1973 (11 March and 23 September) were direct under Ley 19.862, with a majority runoff; the 1951 election under the 1949 Constitution was also direct (dated from a Presidencia de la Nación page; its decree is not yet found). Every other president from 1854 to 1989 was chosen by an electoral college (class electores_presidente). Since 1995 every presidential election is direct.

classes.name: Elección de diputados nacionales
classes.note: The Chamber of Deputies is elected by district (the 23 provinces and the City of Buenos Aires), half every two years for four-year terms (Constitution arts. 45 and 50). Since 1983, closed lists by D'Hondt among lists with 3% of the district's registered voters (Código Electoral arts. 160-161; Ley 22.838); 254 seats in 1983, 257 since Tierra del Fuego became a province, renewed 127 and 130 in alternation. Earlier systems: the complete list, single-member districts in 1904 (Ley 4.161), the incomplete list of the Sáenz Peña law from 1912 (Ley 8.871), single-member circumscriptions in 1951 and 1954 (Ley 14.032), and proportional representation from 1963. Each district's election counts as one contest; dates are those DINE prints on each district's sheet.

classes.note: Constitution art. 40 (1994) and Ley 25.432 let Congress call a binding consulta and Congress or the president a non-binding one. classes.name: Elección de gobernador y vicegobernador, y de jefe de Gobierno de la Ciudad
classes.name_en: Gubernatorial elections (and Head of Government of the City of Buenos Aires)
classes.note: Governor and vice governor on one ticket in each of the 23 provinces, and the Head of Government of the City of Buenos Aires, elected since 30 June 1996 (Ley 24.620; Decree 50/96). Four-year terms. Most provinces elect by plurality; the City (absolute majority), Chaco and Corrientes (45%, or 40% with a 10-point lead), and Tierra del Fuego (absolute majority) hold runoffs. Provinces set their own days, some with the national election and many apart. In the 19th century and until 1912 many governors were chosen by legislatures or provincial electoral colleges; those choices are not enumerated. All 22 provinces elected governors with the national election of 30 October 1983; Tierra del Fuego from 1991. Each dated row's regions count its contests by province, keyed by the ISO 3166-2:AR letter (B Buenos Aires, C City of Buenos Aires, and so on).

classes.name_en: Provincial legislature and lower chamber elections
classes.note: Sixteen jurisdictions have one chamber (the City of Buenos Aires, Chaco, Chubut, Córdoba, Formosa, Jujuy, La Pampa, La Rioja, Misiones, Neuquén, Río Negro, San Juan, Santa Cruz, Santiago del Estero, Tierra del Fuego, and Tucumán) and eight two (Buenos Aires, Catamarca, Corrientes, Entre Ríos, Mendoza, Salta, San Luis, and Santa Fe); this class holds the single and lower chambers, 1,018 of the 1,201 provincial seats (DNE). Systems range from list PR by province or section to mixed systems (Córdoba, Río Negro, San Juan), with half or whole renewals. Each dated row's regions count its contests by province, keyed by the ISO 3166-2:AR letter (B Buenos Aires, C City of Buenos Aires, and so on).

classes.note: Each of the 135 partidos of Buenos Aires province elects a consejo escolar with its council, by list PR (Ley 14.249 apportions "Concejales y Consejeros Escolares"). The Junta Electoral's CSVs carry the category by partido from 2003.

dates.note: Municipal elections are not yet enumerated by province.

access.platform: Junta Electoral de la Provincia de Buenos Aires
access.evidence: CSV per partido and election from 2003, by list and office; no votes by polling table

classes.name: Elección de tribunales de cuentas municipales y comunales de Córdoba
classes.name_en: Córdoba municipal and communal audit court elections
classes.note: Córdoba's municipalities and comunas elect their own tribunales de cuentas with the intendente and council (the Justicia Electoral's 2023 application lists Tribunal de Cuentas Municipal and Comunal).

dates.note: Municipal elections are not yet enumerated by province.

access.platform: Justicia Electoral de la Provincia de Córdoba
access.evidence: Report applications for 2003-2023 by department, circuit, and locality; 2001 as PDF certificates

classes.name: Elección de convencionales municipales
classes.note: Municipalities with autonomy elect conventions to write or reform their charters (cartas orgánicas), for example 232 municipal convention members in Salta on 11 May 2025; Santa Fe provides for them in Ley 14.478.

dates.note: Not yet enumerated.

dates.quote: se votarán 232 convencionales municipales, que estarán encargados de reformar las cartas orgánicas de sus distritos
dates.note: Salta; the number of municipalities is not given.

classes.name: Consultas populares municipales
classes.note: Municipal charters and laws provide for consultas and plebiscites; none is yet cited from an official source (the 2003 Esquel plebiscite on mining is known only from secondary sources).

classes.name: Elección de juntas comunales de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires
classes.name_en: City of Buenos Aires community board elections
classes.note: Each of the 15 comunas elects a seven-member Junta Comunal (105 seats) by list PR for four years with the Head of Government (Ley 1777 art. 19): 2011, 2015, 2019, and 2023.

dates.quote: Miembros de Junta Comunal electos ... Año 2011

dates.note: 2015, 2019, and 2023 not yet counted.

classes.name: Elecciones internas de partidos
classes.disposition_reason: Party-internal votes that the parties run under their own charters; the state-run primaries are the classes paso and paso_provincial.
classes.note: Internal elections of party authorities, and candidate selection in provinces without state-run primaries, where the DNE notes "No hay PASO. A criterio de los partidos".

classes.name: Consejo de la Magistratura y otros cuerpos de elección estamental
classes.name_en: Judicial council and other peer-elected bodies
classes.disposition_reason: Not public elections: judges, lawyers, and academics elect their own members of the national Consejo de la Magistratura (Constitution art. 114), and bar, union, and university bodies vote under their own rules. Chubut's popularly elected council members are in class judicial.

classes.name: Comisiones y juntas vecinales
classes.disposition_reason: Neighborhood commissions and centros vecinales are civil associations whose votes municipalities supervise under ordinances; no electoral authority runs or publishes them.
